subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the public API be a nested/per-agent `ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` style policy instead of the requested top-level key?
rationale: The source shows the primitive exists, but exposing it changes an SSRF security boundary and the current maintainer discussion rejects the first top-level shape without settling the final public contract.

options.title: Adopt Nested Audited Policy
options.body: Use a nested `web_fetch` SSRF policy, ideally per-agent, with explicit dangerous naming, audit warnings, docs, cache separation, and redirect/metadata tests.

options.title: Accept Simple Global Toggle
options.body: Expose a simpler global private-network switch and explicitly own the larger blast radius and future migration cost.

options.title: Reject Broad Private Access
options.body: Keep arbitrary `web_fetch` strict and direct users to trusted proxies, narrow fake-IP flags, or purpose-specific tools for internal services.

recommendation.title: Adopt Nested Audited Policy
recommendation.body: Use a nested `web_fetch` SSRF policy, ideally per-agent, with explicit dangerous naming, audit warnings, docs, cache separation, and redirect/metadata tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible combination of prior SSRF/web_fetch implementation history and maintainer-context review on the rejected top-level shape.
